cite_runs: – A DISSERTATION SUBMITTED TO THE GRADUATE DIVISION OF THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAI‘I AT MĀNOA IN PARTIAL FULFILLMENT OF THE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE DEGREE OF DOCTOR OF PHILOSOPHY IN URBAN AND REGIONAL PLANNING “HOW CAN LAWS, INSTITUTIONS, AND PLANS FACILITATE ALASKA NATIVE VILLAGE ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE CHANGE?” Proquest  //DH
body: Despite the desire for more external financial assistance,
participants said they felt exploited by
lack of power relative to outside
and a few said that the outside government should step back
and take cues from the ANV communities. One supporter of indigenous rights from a federal agency conveyed this sense of exploitation:
he US government has been involved, influencing the indigenous peoples’ inherent rights

now…I’m not sure that …solutions we come up with…are the right solutions. I’m not sure that …it’s best to leave it up to the policy influencers and lobbyists in DC but if the federal policy makers took a true listen to ANVs on what their needs are, a better solution could be drawn.
One ANV resident wanted to convey this message to federal
They get in there and just screw everything up for us …. Everything they tell us to do, we’ve been doing for 14,000 years
. And we can do it for another 14,000 years.”
